messages.author: 86b74f7212a0aefa
messages.subject: assocComp methylBaseDB problem
parts:
Dear all,

Maybe I found a bug or I am doing something wrong. To provide you with a reproducible data set however, I also need some input (please see below).

I get problems running assocComp with an object from a methylBaseDB class . I get this error. 
Error in rbindlist(res) : 
  Item 1 of list input is not a data.frame, data.table or list

This is contrary to what the manual says ->" methylBase or methylBaseDB object with no NA values in the data part." Therefore the methylBaseDB should work. 

Subsetting this methylBaseDB to methylBase than works fine and also doesn't give any error anymore. Therefore my workaround and my solution to this  error message above, is to save my methylBaseDB as methylBase with pretending to subset my data methylBaseDB but without removing anything (-> subset2=my.methylBaseDB.obj.[,]) 

But maybe it is really a bug? Is there a way to subset a DB to a smaller DB? Or to save smaller subset-methylBase to a new methylBaseDB? Or to simulate a methylBaseDB.obj?? So I can provide you with an small methylBaseDB? And we can check together what is causing the error message?

Thanks a lot, 
Britta

messages.author: a413e6cf6c4ea2cc
messages.subject: Re: assocComp methylBaseDB problem
parts:
Hi Britta,

You were right, this is a bug if input is a methylBaseDB, I will follow up on this!

In our latest documentation on bioconductor you can find descriptions of the functions you required to subset your data (here). 
So in general we do not provide a direct way to subset a DB into a smaller DB (to avoid writing to many files),
so the subset will be a normal (nonDB) object. But what you can do is to use the function makeMethylDB(), 
which can create the methylDB pendant for your corresponding input object. 

Same holds for the simulation, you can use makeMethylDB() on the result of the dataSim() function, which can simulate the data for a methylBase object. 

If you have any further questions, or need more details please ask!


Best Alex
